title: Join strings into a new buffer
description:
Write `char *join_new(const char *sep, ...)` that joins any number of strings, ended by a `NULL` argument, into a newly allocated string with `sep` between them. The caller frees the result. With no strings it returns an empty string `""` (allocated). If `malloc` fails it returns `NULL`.

```c
char *s = join_new(", ", "red", "green", "blue", (const char *)NULL);   /* "red, green, blue" */
```

Walk the arguments twice with `va_copy`: once to work out the exact length, once to copy. Then write `char *format_new(const char *format, ...)` that returns a newly allocated string formatted like `printf`, sized exactly with `vsnprintf(NULL, 0, ...)`.
hints: Two passes over the arguments need two `va_list`s: `va_copy(again, args)` right after `va_start`, walk `args` to measure, walk `again` to copy, and `va_end` both.
The length is the sum of the string lengths plus the separator once between each pair: `strlen(sep) * (count - 1)` when there are at least two strings. Add 1 for the terminating zero.
